summary: __str__ sets the text print() shows for your object, and __eq__ sets what == means. Use is only when you need to know if two names point to the same object.
notes: return NotImplemented tells Python the comparison does not apply, so a == 1001 becomes False.
b in roster calls __eq__ on each item, so it finds a matching Student by id.
Defining __eq__ removes the default __hash__, so you also need __hash__ to put a Student in a set or use it as a dict key.
pitfall: Using is to compare two students with the same data gives False, because is checks identity. Use == to compare values.
